content:
incident-bot: PAGER: tensor/pipeline collective errors detected on prod-gpu-pool-7. Alert: repeated NCCL communicator resets + container restarts. impact: some TP jobs stalled, increased 95th latency for streaming requests. link: https://incident.internal/1763159876 :rotating_light:
ryan (oncall): ack. I'm on it. Which jobs are impacted? any customer hits?
kai (eng-runtime): seeing repeated 'NCCL WARN Transport failed: Unreachable' followed by 'GPU0: CudaError: out of memory' in the same timeline. Logs from runtime node gpu-7a attached to the incident page.
linda (sre): node telemetry shows GPU fan tach spiking and an unclean driver reset ~3x over last 10min. dmesg shows 'NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus'. suspect hardware flapping + NCCL timeouts.
devin (prodops): I'm pulling the node out of the pool now (draining new tasks). can we migrate active sessions off that node?
kai (eng-runtime): yes — starting immediate reroute for any TP shards on gpu-7a to fallback model variants on single-gpu replicas. applying route policy: prefer single-gpu variant with quantized profile.
cs-jordan: AcmeCorp reported timeouts on our streaming endpoint ~09:12, they say partial outputs then stalls. they're on a live demo. please flag customer impact.
ryan (oncall): noted — @cs-jordan please send an update to AcmeCorp that we're investigating and have a mitigation in place (fallback routing). target ETA to restore interactive performance 10-15m.
infra-bot: evacuation started: cordon node gpu-7a -> drain pods -> relocate PVs.
kai (eng-runtime): quick mitigation checklist I'm running through: 1) drain node 2) force fallback routing for TP jobs 3) disable multi-node collectives for in-flight jobs where possible 4) bump NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 on runtime group 5) increase NCCL_TIMEOUT to 5000 for remaining clusters.
linda (sre): agree on steps 1-3. careful with changing NCCL_TIMEOUT wide-scale — can mask root cause. I'd prefer targeted env changes on the affected worker pool only.
ryan (oncall): deploy plan: kai -> apply routing change + env to runtime-pool-prod-7 (canary 10% jobs) -> if stable, rollout to 100%. linda -> continue node removal and hardware checks. devin -> stand by to reprovision replacement node.
kai (eng-runtime): implementing canary now. command: ```kubectl set env ds/runtime-serving -n prod NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 --selector=pool=prod-7``` pushing canary to 10% traffic. watching logs.
(2m later) kai (eng-runtime): canary looks good so far, no further communicator resets on canary pods. latency on those requests back to baseline.
linda (sre): node gpu-7a is offline for maintenance, NV driver reloaded, vendor oncall notified. RAID controller reported no faults.
devin (prodops): replacement node provisioning started (type: a100-80g). ETA 18m.
ryan (oncall): running customer impact assessment: affected customers: AcmeCorp (high priority), 2 internal batch jobs delayed (low impact). no data loss observed — KV caches persisted.
cs-jordan: I'll message AcmeCorp: short note explaining transient GPU failure, mitigation applied (fallback to single-gpu model), ETA 15-20m for full restoration. include invite for postmortem if they want deeper details.
kai (eng-runtime): follow-up: logs show a race between NCCL rendezvous and CUDA OOM when node started flapping; plausible sequence: driver drop -> partial communicator shutdown -> NDAC (sic) attempts to reconnect -> timeouts -> OOM as shards redistributed. investigating patch to reduce concurrent shard migrations.
linda (sre): adding temporary guard: limit simultaneous shard reschedules to 2 per host to avoid OOM storms. applying to scheduler config for prod-7 pool only.
dry: reaction added by ryan (oncall): :thumbsup:
ryan (oncall): OK. current status: fallback routing at 100% for impacted job classes, node drained and under vendor repair, replacement node provisioning in flight, canary env change stable. escalating to eng-runtime for longer-term fix. please update the incident page and I'll start the handoff doc for the oncall who takes the night shift.
kai (eng-runtime): opened ticket INF-2342 for runtime patch (limit concurrent shard migrations + better NCCL error handling). assigned to Kai + Linda.
ryan (oncall): Linda, please prepare short runbook blurb for oncall handoff: detection signals, immediate mitigation commands, customer notification text. I'll hand off at 18:00 PST.
linda (sre): on it. will add commands and the quick checks (dmesg GPU falloff, nvidia-smi driver resets, kubectl describe pod for OOMKilled).
cs-jordan: AcmeCorp replied — they saw partial outputs come back after fallback, asked for an incident timeline. I'll sync with you all after you post an initial summary.
ryan (oncall): thanks. marking this thread as active incident. will update again in 10m or on any major change.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: active -> mitigated (partial). linked ticket INF-2342.
